**Finding submitted: MISSING (insurance)**

**What I found.** The Agreement has no insurance provision at all — a document-wide search for "insurance" returned zero hits, and Section 10 (General Provisions, p0059–p0070) runs from Notices, No Joint Venture, Assignment, Waiver, Governing Law, Severability, Survival, Entire Agreement through Headings/Counterparts without any coverage requirement.

**Why it matters here.** HDI is unambiguously a hosting/services vendor to us, so the rule is triggered on its facts:
- Sections 1.1/1.3/1.4 — HDI designs, develops, operates and hosts the Site on its own server and system.
- Section 1.5 — HDI collects customer orders and processes our inventory import/export files.
- Section 8.1 — HDI expressly acknowledges access to our "Content, user information, data, knowledge and proprietary and trade secret information."

A vendor hosting our consumer storefront and processing order and user data with zero insurance backstop is the playbook's walk-away scenario, not merely a gap. I also confirmed the direction is correct: the new obligation runs against HDI (counterparty), not us.

**The edit.** A single new Section 10.9 inserted after p0070 — CGL USD 1M per occurrence / 2M aggregate, E&O USD 2M, cyber/privacy USD 5M, statutory workers' compensation, term plus one year, certificates on request. Placing it at the end of Section 10 has a useful side benefit: Section 10.7's survival language already carries all of Section 10 for two years post-termination, so the tail coverage is reinforced without extra drafting.

Two notes for the negotiation, since I made judgment calls:
1. I tied the cyber limit to HDI "processing Confidential Information, user information and data hereunder" rather than importing a "Customer Data" defined term, because this Agreement has no such definition — Section 8.1's Confidential Information is the operative concept.
2. The planner flagged a possible affiliate-relationship carve-out. I did not act on it: Section 10.2 states the parties are independent contractors and expressly disclaims partnership, joint venture and agency, so nothing in the document supports softening the requirement on affiliate grounds. If HDI raises an intra-group insurance program in response, the recorded fallback (E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M) is the place to land.
